newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: China envisions "new Hong Kong" in northeast Asia.
newsitem.headline: China envisions "new Hong Kong" in northeast Asia.

text.p: An ambitious $30 billion joint development project between six northeast Asian countries in the Tumen river area straddling North Korea and China could produce an economic miracle such as Hong Kong, a Chinese academic said on Tuesday.

The Tumen River Economic Development Area, which aims to set up a world-class free port and free trade zone on the Sea of Japan, would create a booming metropolis, China's Ye Shunzan told the seventh meeting of the Northeast Asia Economic Forum.
"Tumenjiang City may develop along the lines of Hong Kong," said Ye, of China's Academy of Sciences, in a reference to the rapid economic growth of the former British colony.

"The village... could grow to a metropolis of one million people in about 30 years," Ye said, referring to the town of 6,000 people at the mouth of the Tumen river in northeast China and which will form part of the zone.
The zone could follow Hong Kong's example, focusing first on shipping and entrepot trading and then switching to manufacturing and export-oriented industries, he said.
The zone is being developed by the three contiguous countries -- China, North Korea and Russia -- as well as by Japan, Mongolia, and South Korea.

Ye said the favorable location of the lower reaches of the Tumen river, boasting abundant natural resources and a potential market of over 300 million people, would ensure the area became a focal point for development where large quantities of goods would be produced and transported.
The area could become an international centre for transportation, communications, trade, manufacturing, finance, the information industry and tourism, Ye said.
"It should be jointly developed and managed as a free port city," Ye said, adding that problems were inevitable.
The Tumen programme has been troubled by political differences, with China and South Korea championing the project, but other participants more reluctant to move forward.
"If the related countries have the political will to realise the programme's goals, it will succeed," Ye said.
"The best way to develop Tumenjiang City and its surroundings is to first develop the transport and communications sectors and resource-oriented processing industries," he said.
A railway link to Mongolia should be built as soon as possible to transport its abundant mineral resources and livestock to overseas markets, Ye said.
